mainTopic: Blessings over food and the search for their source
overview: The משנה lists the blessings over food: tree fruit, wine, produce of the ground, bread, and vegetables, where רבי יהודה gives a different wording. The גמרא asks for a source for blessings and suggests the verse קֹדֶשׁ הִלּוּלִים, but that verse seems to be needed for the laws of fourth-year fruit. For the view of כֶּרֶם רְבָעִי, a גזרה שוה frees one הִלּוּל to teach a ברכה after eating. A קל וחומר then adds the ברכה before eating. The גמרא tries to extend the rule to all foods, first from vineyard and grain through הצד השוה and then from the שבעת המינין, but each attempt is refuted. Since no verse covers foods that are not planted, like meat, eggs, and fish, the גמרא concludes that the ברכה is a סברא: one may not enjoy this world without a ברכה. A ברייתא calls such enjoyment מעילה, and רבא explains that one should learn ברכות from a חכם in advance. שמואל and רבי לוי add that the world belongs to ה׳ before a ברכה, and רבי לוי's answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Blessings for tree fruit and wine
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives the usual blessing for tree fruit and a distinct blessing for wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does one bless over fruit? For tree fruit one says “Creator of the fruit of the tree”; for wine one says “Creator of the fruit of the vine.”
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with a question and gives its first set of rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine comes from fruit of a tree, but the משנה gives it its own wording. The exception changes the blessing, not wine’s origin.

phrases.english: Mishna: How does one bless over fruits?
For tree fruits, one says:
“Creator of the fruit of the tree,” except for wine,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁעַל הַיַּיִן הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הַגֶּפֶן״.
phrases.english: for over wine one says: “Creator of the fruit of the vine.”

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tree fruit receives בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הָעֵץ; wine receives its own blessing.

steps.title: Blessings for produce of the ground and bread
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives the usual blessing for ground-grown produce and a distinct blessing for bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: For fruits of the ground one says “Creator of the fruit of the ground,” except for bread, over which one says “Who brings forth bread from the earth.”
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list of blessings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bread follows the same pattern as wine in the previous rule: it receives special blessing wording. The משנה does not remove it from the broader group of foods produced from the ground.

keyTerms.meaning: the blessing for produce of the ground

phrases.english: And for fruits of the ground one says:
“Creator of the fruit of the ground,” except for bread,
for over bread one says:
“Who brings forth bread from the earth.”

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ground-grown produce receives בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הָאֲדָמָה; bread receives its own blessing.

steps.title: A disagreement about vegetables
steps.stepSummary: The first opinion uses the ground-produce blessing for vegetables; רבי יהודה gives them different wording.
steps.simpleTranslation: For vegetables one says “Creator of the fruit of the ground.” רבי יהודה says: “Creator of kinds of grasses.”
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list with a disagreement about vegetables.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion keeps vegetables under the blessing already given for ground-grown produce. רבי יהודה gives vegetables a more specific blessing.

phrases.english: And for vegetables one says:
“Creator of the fruit of the ground.”
Rabbi Yehuda says:
“Creator of kinds of grasses.”

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first opinion says בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הָאֲדָמָה over vegetables; רבי יהודה says בּוֹרֵא מִינֵי דְשָׁאִים.

steps.title: Where do blessings over food come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the blessing requirement.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know these matters?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from listing blessings to asking for their source. This question sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question does not yet distinguish among the foods in the משנה. It begins with the more basic issue of why one blesses.

phrases.english: Gemara: From where do we know these matters?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source for blessing over food.

steps.title: A verse is offered as a source for blessings
steps.stepSummary: A teaching reads קֹדֶשׁ הִלּוּלִים as requiring a blessing before and after.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: “Holy for praises to the Lord” teaches that blessings are required before and after.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the source question by quoting an earlier teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching connects the verse’s language of praise to blessings. At this point, the verse is being offered as a source for both before and after.

phrases.english: For the Sages taught: “Holy for praises to the Lord,”
teaches that they require a blessing before them and after them.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A teaching derives blessings before and after from קֹדֶשׁ הִלּוּלִים.

steps.title: One must bless before tasting
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא states the practical rule drawn from the teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here רבי עקיבא said: A person may not taste anything before blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The text adds רבי עקיבא’s rule about tasting food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This rule focuses on the blessing before eating. It is stated as a result of the preceding teaching, before the גמרא tests that teaching’s reading of the verse.

phrases.english: From here Rabbi Akiva said:
A person is forbidden to taste anything
before blessing.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person must bless before tasting anything.

steps.title: The verse may be needed for redemption
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proposed source: קֹדֶשׁ הִלּוּלִים appears to teach rules about redeeming fourth-year fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did “holy for praises” come for that? It is needed to teach, first, redeem it and then eat it; and second, something requiring song requires redemption, while something not requiring song does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the use of the verse as a source for blessings. It points to two other teachings drawn from the verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first teaching requires redemption before eating. The second links redemption to something accompanied by song; the next steps explain why wine fits that description.

phrases.english: And did this “holy for praises” come for that purpose?
This is needed, first,
because the Merciful One said: Redeem it and then eat it.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִידָךְ דָּבָר הַטָּעוּן שִׁירָה, טָעוּן חִלּוּל,
phrases.english: And second: Something requiring song requires redemption,

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁאֵינוֹ טָעוּן שִׁירָה, אֵין טָעוּן חִלּוּל.
phrases.english: and something not requiring song does not require redemption.

steps.kashyaTarget: The use of קֹדֶשׁ הִלּוּלִים as the source for blessings.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse appears to be needed to teach redemption and its connection to song.

steps.title: Why is wine linked to song?
steps.stepSummary: A cited teaching asks for the source that song is said only over wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this follows רבי שמואל בר נחמני in the name of רבי יונתן, who asked: From where do we know that song is said only over wine?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings in a teaching to explain the song-and-redemption point. Its question sets up the proof that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous step spoke about something that requires song without yet identifying its source. This question narrows the discussion to wine.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִדְרַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן
phrases.english: And as Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said in the name of Rabbi Yonatan

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן:
phrases.english: for Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said in the name of Rabbi Yonatan:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵין אוֹמְרִים שִׁירָה אֶלָּא עַל הַיַּיִן? —
phrases.english: From where do we know that song is said only over wine? —

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִדְרַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for saying song only over wine.

steps.title: A verse connects wine with song
steps.stepSummary: A verse says wine gladdens God and people; the teaching explains the reference to God through song over wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: The vine says that its wine gladdens God and people. If its effect on people is clear, how does it gladden God? From here, song is said only over wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The cited teaching answers its question with a verse and an inference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question “How does it gladden God?” is part of the proof, not a new challenge to it. The answer uses the verse to connect wine with song in the Temple service.

phrases.english: As it is stated: “And the vine said to them,

phrases.aramaic: הֶחֳדַלְתִּי אֶת תִּירוֹשִׁי הַמְשַׂמֵּחַ אֱלֹהִים וַאֲנָשִׁים״,
phrases.english: Should I give up my wine, which gladdens God and people?”

phrases.aramaic: אִם אֲנָשִׁים מְשַׂמֵּחַ, אֱלֹהִים בַּמֶּה מְשַׂמֵּחַ?
phrases.english: If it gladdens people, in what way does it gladden God?

phrases.aramaic: מִכָּאן שֶׁאֵין אוֹמְרִים שִׁירָה אֶלָּא עַל הַיַּיִן!
phrases.english: From here we learn that song is said only over wine!

steps.raayaObject: Song is said only over wine.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The verse describing wine as gladdening God and people.

steps.title: The fourth-year grapevine view creates a difficulty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא distinguishes between a view about all fourth-year tree fruit and a view specifically about fourth-year grapevines.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for the one who teaches “fourth-year sapling.” But what can be said for the one who teaches “fourth-year grapevine”?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the proposed source for blessings and raises a more focused difficulty. It asks how that source works for the view limited to grapevines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the law already covers fourth-year tree fruit generally, the wine-only link to song need not serve to limit which fruit is redeemed. For the grapevine view, that link has a job, making it harder to use the same verse for blessings.

phrases.english: This works for the one who teaches “fourth-year sapling.”
But for the one who teaches “fourth-year grapevine,”
what can be said?

steps.kashyaTarget: The availability of קֹדֶשׁ הִלּוּלִים as a source for blessings under the grapevine-specific view.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That view has reason to use the song-related reading to establish its grapevine-specific redemption rule.

steps.title: Two versions of the fourth-year rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא identifies the two wordings behind its question.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי—one taught “fourth-year grapevine,” and one taught “fourth-year sapling.”
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supplies the reported disagreement that its question relies on. This sets up further discussion of the two views.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The report establishes that both wordings were taught. This passage does not say which named teacher used which wording, and it does not yet answer the question raised in the previous step.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִתְּמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרַבִּי,
phrases.english: As it was stated: Rabbi Ḥiyya and Rabbi Shimon, son of Rabbi,
one taught “fourth-year grapevine,”
and one taught “fourth-year sapling.”

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִתְּמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרַבִּי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two versions of the fourth-year rule are reported: כֶּרֶם רְבָעִי and נֶטַע רְבָעִי.

steps.title: The vineyard view works if he learns a verbal analogy
steps.stepSummary: For the one who teaches כֶּרֶם רְבָעִי, the derivation of ברכה from הִלּוּלִים works, as long as he learns a גזרה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the person who teaches 'a fourth-year vineyard,' things work out fine, if he learns this from a גזרה שוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to answer its question for the view of כֶּרֶם רְבָעִי. It says this view has no problem if he learns a גזרה שוה, and the next step will bring that גזרה שוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The view of כֶּרֶם רְבָעִי holds that the fourth-year law applies only to grapes. If that limit comes from a separate גזרה שוה, then the word הִלּוּלִים is not needed to teach it. The word is then free to teach ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: A vineyard in its fourth year; this wording limits the law to grapes
It works out well; there is no problem
A verbal analogy: the same word in two places links their laws

phrases.english: And according to the one who teaches 'fourth-year vineyard'
it works out well if he derives it from a verbal analogy.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּתָנֵי כֶּרֶם רְבָעִי הָנִיחָא אִי יָלֵיף גְּזֵרָה שָׁוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from steps 7 and 10–11 for the view of כֶּרֶם רְבָעִי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Conditional resolution: the limit to vineyards comes from another source.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both uses of הִלּוּלִים are taken up by the laws of fourth-year fruit, so none is left for ברכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: If the limit to vineyards comes from a גזרה שוה, one הִלּוּל is freed.

steps.title: רבי's verbal analogy: produce means a vineyard
steps.stepSummary: רבי links the word תְּבוּאָה in the verse about young trees to תְּבוּאַת הַכָּרֶם in the verse about mixed planting. This shows the law is about vineyards.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי says, it says here 'to increase for you its produce,' and it says there 'and the produce of the vineyard.' Just as there it means a vineyard, so too here it means a vineyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that holds the גזרה שוה it just mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about a tree's early years uses the word תְּבוּאָתוֹ, 'its produce.' The verse about כִּלְאַיִם uses תְּבוּאַת הַכָּרֶם, 'the produce of the vineyard.' The shared word teaches that the fourth-year law is about vineyards.

keyTerms.meaning: It says here... and it says there: the standard opening of a גזרה שוה
Produce; the shared word that links the two verses
Just as there... so too here

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rebbi says:
It is stated here: 'to increase for you its produce,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא יט:כה, about the fruit of a young tree.

phrases.english: and it is stated there: 'and the produce of the vineyard.'

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְהַלָּן כֶּרֶם, אַף כָּאן כֶּרֶם.
phrases.english: Just as there it is a vineyard, so too here it is a vineyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the גזרה שוה that step 12 depended on.
steps.raayaObject: That the fourth-year law is limited to vineyards without using הִלּוּלִים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי: a גזרה שוה from תְּבוּאָתוֹ and תְּבוּאַת הַכָּרֶם.

steps.title: One extra word remains to teach a blessing
steps.stepSummary: Because the גזרה שוה limits the law to vineyards, one הִלּוּל is left over to teach ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: So he has one extra 'praise' left over, for a ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes this line of thought. For this view, one הִלּוּל is free, so ברכה can be learned from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גזרה שוה now does the job of limiting the law to vineyards, so a הִלּוּל no longer has to do it. The leftover word becomes the source for ברכה over food.

keyTerms.meaning: It is left over or extra
Praise; one of the two praise-words in קֹדֶשׁ הִלּוּלִים

phrases.english: One 'praise' is left over for him, for the blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the result from רבי's גזרה שוה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For the view of כֶּרֶם רְבָעִי that learns the גזרה שוה, the extra הִלּוּל teaches ברכה.

steps.title: Without the verbal analogy, where is the blessing from?
steps.stepSummary: If he does not learn the גזרה שוה, both הִלּוּלִים are used up. So where does he learn ברכה?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he does not learn the גזרה שוה, where does he learn ברכה from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. It works only for someone who accepts the גזרה שוה, so what about someone who does not?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the גזרה שוה, one הִלּוּל is needed to limit the law to vineyards. Both words are then taken, and none is free for ברכה. The גמרא does not answer this directly; in the end it drops the verse sources and bases ברכה on a סברא (step 34).

keyTerms.meaning: Where does he get it from?

phrases.english: And if he does not derive the verbal analogy,
where does he derive the blessing from?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי לָא יָלֵיף גְּזֵרָה שָׁוָה בְּרָכָה מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the conditional answer from steps 12–14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the view of כֶּרֶם רְבָעִי has a source for ברכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The answer depends on the גזרה שוה. Without it, both הִלּוּלִים are used up.

steps.title: Even with the verbal analogy, what about the blessing before eating?
steps.stepSummary: Even if he learns the גזרה שוה, the leftover הִלּוּל only shows a ברכה after eating. Where is the source for a ברכה before eating?
steps.simpleTranslation: And even if he learns the גזרה שוה, we found a ברכה after eating. Where do we learn a ברכה before eating?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a second problem. Even in the best case, the source only teaches a ברכה after eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original ברייתא learned two ברכות, before and after, from the plural הִלּוּלִים. Now only one הִלּוּל is left over, so it can teach only one ברכה, and that one is matched to the known ברכה after eating, like ברכת המזון. The ברכה before eating still has no source.

keyTerms.meaning: Before it, from where? (the ברכה before eating)

phrases.english: And even if he does derive the verbal analogy,
we have found a source for the blessing after eating;
for the blessing before eating, from where?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי נָמֵי יָלֵיף גְּזֵרָה שָׁוָה אַשְׁכְּחַן לְאַחֲרָיו לְפָנָיו מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate challenge to the same answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: How much the extra הִלּוּל actually covers.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two ברכות came from the plural הִלּוּלִים. With only one הִלּוּל left over, only one ברכה, the one after eating, has a source.

steps.title: The blessing before eating comes from a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: If one says a ברכה when full, then surely one must say a ברכה when hungry.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult, because it comes from a קל וחומר. If when he is full he says a ברכה, then when he is hungry, all the more so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second problem. The ברכה before eating follows by logic from the ברכה after eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A full person has less reason to feel he needs God, and he still says a ברכה. A hungry person, about to get the food he needs, has even more reason to say one. So once the ברכה after eating is known, the ברכה before eating follows.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from the lighter case to the stronger case

steps.confusionAlert: This answer solves only the second problem (step 16), the ברכה before eating. The first problem (step 15), about someone who does not learn the גזרה שוה, gets no direct answer; it falls away when the גמרא bases ברכה on a סברא (step 34).

phrases.english: This is not difficult,
since it comes from an a fortiori argument:
when he is full, he blesses;
when he is hungry, all the more so.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא דְּאָתְיָא בְּקַל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the ברכה after eating has a source.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברכה before eating follows from the ברכה after eating by קל וחומר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This קל וחומר is a well-known argument for why we say a ברכה before eating, and the idea comes up again in later discussions.

steps.title: What about foods other than grapes?
steps.stepSummary: The source so far covers only produce of the vineyard. Where do we learn ברכה for other kinds of food?
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a source for the vineyard. For other kinds of food, from where?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the source covers only grapes. It asks for a source for other foods, setting up the next part of the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source is a verse about a fourth-year vineyard, so it teaches a ברכה only over grapes. The גמרא now needs a way to extend the rule to all foods.
steps.whatToRemember: For the view of כֶּרֶם רְבָעִי: the גזרה שוה frees one הִלּוּל, which teaches a ברכה after eating. A קל וחומר adds the ברכה before eating. But all of this so far covers only grapes.

phrases.english: We have found a source for the vineyard;
for other kinds of produce, from where?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the source found so far and asks to widen it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source for saying a ברכה over foods other than grapes.

steps.title: Learning from the vineyard to all foods
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we learn from כרם: just as vineyard produce gives enjoyment and needs a ברכה, so too every food that gives enjoyment needs a ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from the vineyard. A vineyard gives a person enjoyment and needs a ברכה. So too, anything that gives a person enjoyment needs a ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 18 by comparing all foods to the vineyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vineyard is treated as a model case (בנין אב). The feature that seems to cause the ברכה is enjoyment, and every food has that feature. So the rule should spread to every food.

phrases.english: For he learns it from the vineyard:
Just as a vineyard is an item one enjoys
and it requires a blessing,
so too any item one enjoys
requires a blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18 about foods other than grapes.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A בנין אב from כרם: enjoyment plus ברכה in a vineyard teaches ברכה for every food one enjoys.

steps.title: The vineyard is special because of leftover grape clusters
steps.stepSummary: The comparison can be broken: a vineyard has the special law of עוללות, so maybe its ברכה is also a special law that does not apply to other foods.
steps.simpleTranslation: This can be refuted. What about a vineyard? It is special, because it must give עוללות to the poor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the comparison from step 19 by pointing out something unique about vineyards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A comparison only works if the model case is not special. A vineyard has an extra מצוה‎, עוללות, that other produce does not have. So maybe the ברכה is also an extra strictness that applies only to vineyards.

keyTerms.meaning: What about X? It is special because...
Small, incomplete grape clusters left for the poor

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying that עוללות causes the ברכה. It only says that a vineyard is a special case, so we cannot safely copy its laws onto everything else.

phrases.english: This can be refuted:
What about a vineyard, which is obligated in olelot!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the בנין אב of step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison from כרם to all foods.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A model case with a unique strictness (עוללות) cannot teach a general rule, because its ברכה might also be a unique strictness.

steps.title: Standing grain proves the point
steps.stepSummary: Standing grain (קמה) has no עוללות but still needs a ברכה, so עוללות is not the reason for the ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Standing grain will prove it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by bringing a second model case, grain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grain (bread) needs a ברכה from the תורה, ברכת המזון, yet it has no עוללות. That shows a ברכה can exist without עוללות. So the vineyard's special feature does not explain its ברכה.

phrases.english: Standing grain will prove it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counter-example from a second model case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the ברכה depends on the strictness of עוללות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Grain needs a ברכה without עוללות, so עוללות is not the cause.

steps.title: Grain is special because of חלה
steps.stepSummary: Grain also has a unique law, חלה, so maybe its ברכה is a special strictness too.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about standing grain? It is special, because it must have חלה separated from its dough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new model case in the same way it attacked the vineyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grain has its own extra מצוה‎, חלה, which other foods do not have. So grain is also a special case. Its ברכה might come from that special status.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of dough given to a כהן

phrases.english: What about standing grain, which is obligated in challah!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof from קמה in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using קמה as a model case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Grain has a unique strictness (חלה), so its ברכה may also be unique to it.

steps.title: The vineyard proves the point back
steps.stepSummary: A vineyard has no חלה but still needs a ברכה, so חלה is not the reason for the ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The vineyard will prove it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by going back to the vineyard, which has no חלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grapes need a ברכה even though they have no חלה. So חלה does not cause the ברכה. Each case now cancels out the other's special feature.

phrases.english: The vineyard will prove it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counter-example from the first model case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the ברכה depends on the strictness of חלה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A vineyard needs a ברכה without חלה, so חלה is not the cause.

steps.title: The common feature teaches a ברכה for all foods
steps.stepSummary: Neither case alone works, but what they share is enjoyment and a ברכה. So every food one enjoys requires a ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The argument has come back around. This one is not like that one, and that one is not like this one. What they have in common is that each is a thing one enjoys and each needs a ברכה. So too, anything one enjoys needs a ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up by combining both model cases into one proof, called הצד השוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each special feature (עוללות, חלה) is found in only one of the two cases, so neither can be the reason for the ברכה. The only thing both cases share is enjoyment, so enjoyment must be the reason. That reason applies to every food.

keyTerms.meaning: The argument has come back around
The feature of this one is not like the feature of that one
The common feature (a method of derivation)

steps.whatToRemember: A vineyard alone and grain alone each fail as a source, because each has a special law. Together, through הצד השוה, they seem to show that enjoyment is the reason for a ברכה. The next step challenges this because both share a link to the מזבח, and in the end the גמרא drops this proof.
steps.whyThisMatters: This הצד השוה is the גמרא's attempt to extend the ברכה to all foods, not only bread and grapes. It is attacked in steps 25 and 28 because both sources share a צד מזבח, and in the end it is dropped for a סברא (step 34).

phrases.english: And the argument has come back around:
The aspect of this is not like the aspect of that,
and the aspect of that is not like the aspect of this;
the common feature between them:
each is an item one enjoys and it requires a blessing,
so too any item one enjoys
requires a blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines the two model cases defended in steps 21 and 23 into a final derivation.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Through הצד השוה from כרם and קמה, every food one enjoys requires a ברכה.

steps.title: Vineyard and grain share a link to the altar
steps.stepSummary: The common feature of vineyard and grain is that both are offered on the מזבח. So they can only teach about foods like the olive, which is also offered on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is special about what vineyard and grain have in common? Both have a connection to the altar. So the only food we could learn from them is the olive, which also has a connection to the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the הצד השוה from step 24. Grapes and grain share something special: both are brought on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine is poured as a נסך and grain is brought as a מנחה. Because of this shared feature, their ברכה might come from their holiness, not from the enjoyment of eating. Then the rule could only spread to the olive, whose oil is also used on the מזבח, and not to all foods.

keyTerms.meaning: The common feature shared by two sources, used to learn a general rule
A connection to the altar; the food is used in offerings
Olive; its oil is used in מנחות
Comes, meaning it can be learned or derived

phrases.english: What about the common feature between them?
It has a connection to the altar.
phrases.notes: Wine is used for נסכים and grain for מנחות.

phrases.english: And the olive can also be learned from them
phrases.notes: This way of learning can stretch to include the olive, but nothing beyond it.

phrases.english: since it also has a connection to the altar.
phrases.notes: Olive oil is used in the מנחה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the הצד השוה conclusion reached in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The בנין אב from vineyard and grain that every food one enjoys needs a ברכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both sources share a link to the מזבח, which other foods lack. So the ברכה might come from that link, and the rule only reaches the olive.

steps.title: The olive is already called a vineyard in a verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the olive needs to be learned through the מזבח link. A verse already calls an olive grove a כרם, so it should be included with the vineyard directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we really learn the olive from its altar connection? The verse openly calls it a כרם (vineyard), as it says: 'And he burned from the stacked grain to the standing grain and to the olive vineyard.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a side question. The גמרא asks why we need the מזבח route for the olive at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שופטים, שמשון burns the field and the 'כרם זית'. If an olive grove counts as a כרם, the olive should already be covered by the vineyard source itself, without needing the shared feature.

keyTerms.meaning: Standing grain still in the field

phrases.english: And is the olive learned from its altar connection?
But it is openly called 'kerem' (vineyard)!
As it is written: 'And he burned from the stacked grain'
phrases.notes: שופטים טו:ה, the story of שמשון.

phrases.english: 'to the standing grain and to the olive vineyard.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the claim in step 25 that the olive is learned through its מזבח link.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the olive is included only through צד מזבח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A verse calls an olive grove a כרם, so it should already be included with the vineyard directly.

steps.title: רב פפא: it is only called an olive vineyard
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the olive grove is only called 'כרם זית', never plain 'כרם'. So it is not covered by the vineyard law.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is called 'olive vineyard.' It is never called just 'vineyard' without the word 'olive.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the side question from step 26.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word כרם alone means a grape vineyard. The olive grove only gets that name with the word זית added, so the vineyard law does not include it. That is why the olive still needs the מזבח route, and the attack in step 25 stands.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
It is called 'olive vineyard,'
it is not called plain 'vineyard.'
phrases.notes: Plain כרם is used only for grapes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 26.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The olive grove counts as a כרם and is included with the vineyard.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only plain כרם means vineyard. כרם זית is a different term, so the olive is not covered by the vineyard law.

steps.title: The altar objection still stands
steps.stepSummary: After the side question, the גמרא returns to the main problem. Vineyard and grain share a link to the מזבח, so they cannot teach about all foods.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the problem remains: what is special about their common feature? They both have a connection to the altar!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns from the side question to the main attack from step 25.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא repeats the objection on purpose. The side question about the olive did not solve anything. The בנין אב from vineyard and grain still fails because both have a link to the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case; back to the main point
It is difficult; the objection remains

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new objection. It is the same objection from step 25, repeated after the side question about the olive to show that it still stands.

phrases.english: In any case, it is difficult:
What about the common feature between them?
They have a connection to the altar!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the main line of step 25 after the side question in steps 26 and 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The בנין אב from vineyard and grain.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Their shared link to the מזבח might be the real reason for the ברכה, so other foods cannot be learned from them.

steps.title: A new source: the seven species
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the vineyard and grain source and learns from the שבעת המינין. Just as they are foods one enjoys and need a ברכה, every food one enjoys needs a ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we learn it from the seven species: just as the seven species are things one enjoys and need a blessing, so too everything one enjoys needs a blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up the old source and suggests a new one, the שבעת המינין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists the seven species of ארץ ישראל and then says 'ואכלת ושבעת וברכת', you will eat, be satisfied, and bless. The גמרא treats this as a model: what makes them need a ברכה is the enjoyment, so the rule should apply to every food.

keyTerms.meaning: The seven species of ארץ ישראל: wheat, barley, grapes, figs, pomegranates, olives, dates
That one enjoys or benefits from

phrases.english: Rather, he learns it from the seven species:
phrases.notes: Based on 'ואכלת ושבעת וברכת', which follows the list of the seven species.

phrases.english: Just as the seven species
are things one enjoys and that need a blessing,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כׇּל דָּבָר שֶׁנֶּהֱנֶה טָעוּן בְּרָכָה.
phrases.english: so too, anything one enjoys needs a blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the vineyard and grain source, which failed in step 28.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule comes from the vineyard and grain together.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule comes from the שבעת המינין, which need a ברכה because they are enjoyed.

steps.title: The seven species are special because of first fruits
steps.stepSummary: The שבעת המינין have their own special law: one must bring ביכורים from them. So their ברכה might be special too, and other foods cannot be learned from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is special about the seven species? One must bring first fruits from them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new source from step 29.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the שבעת המינין are brought as ביכורים to the בית המקדש. This extra importance might be why they need a ברכה. If so, foods that are not ביכורים would not be included.

keyTerms.meaning: First fruits brought to the בית המקדש, only from the seven species

phrases.english: What about the seven species?
They are obligated in first fruits!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְשִׁבְעַת הַמִּינִין שֶׁכֵּן חַיָּיבִין בְּבִכּוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source proposed in step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: Learning all foods from the שבעת המינין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The seven species have a special law, ביכורים, that other foods lack. So their ברכה might be special too.

steps.title: This only covers the blessing after eating
steps.stepSummary: A second objection: the seven species verse speaks of a ברכה after eating. It does not teach a ברכה before eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: this works for the blessing after eating, but where do we learn the blessing before eating?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second objection to the seven species source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'ואכלת ושבעת וברכת' come after eating and being satisfied, so they teach a ברכה after the meal. Even if the seven species could serve as a model, there is still no source for the ברכה before eating.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore; adds a second objection
After it; the blessing after eating
Before it; the blessing before eating

steps.whatToRemember: Both attempts so far have problems. The vineyard and grain source fails because of the מזבח link. The seven species source fails because of ביכורים, and it also only teaches the ברכה after eating, not before.

phrases.english: And furthermore:
this works for the blessing after,
but from where do we learn the blessing before?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, separate objection to the source in step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using the seven species verse as the source for every ברכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse speaks only of a ברכה after eating, so it cannot be the source for a ברכה before eating.

steps.title: A blessing before eating is learned by a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The objection that the verse only teaches a ברכה after eating is answered with a קל וחומר: if a full person makes a ברכה, a hungry person surely must.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not a difficulty, because it comes from a קל וחומר: when he is full he makes a ברכה; when he is hungry, all the more so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection from step 31. That objection said the verse only teaches a ברכה after eating. The answer is that the ברכה before eating follows by logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who has already eaten and is satisfied still has to thank ה׳. A person who is hungry and about to get the food he wants has even more reason to thank. So the ברכה before eating is learned from the ברכה after eating with a קל וחומר. This answers only the 'before vs. after' objection. The ביכורים objection from step 30 gets no direct answer; the גמרא soon drops the verse sources and bases ברכה on a סברא (step 34).

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a stronger case
Is it not all the more so?

phrases.english: This is not difficult
for it comes through an a fortiori argument:
when he is full, he makes a blessing;
when he is hungry, is it not all the more so?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא דְּאָתֵי בְּקַל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 31 (the verse speaks of a ברכה after eating, not before).
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical derivation (קל וחומר) fills the gap the verse leaves
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse only gives a source for the ברכה after eating, so there is no source for a ברכה before eating.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברכה before eating is learned from the ברכה after eating with a קל וחומר.

steps.title: What about foods that are not planted, like meat, eggs, and fish?
steps.stepSummary: Even the opinion that learns from נטע רבעי can only cover things that grow from planting. It has no source for meat, eggs, and fish.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who teaches 'נטע רבעי', that works well for anything that is planted. But for things that are not planted, like meat, eggs, and fish, where does he learn it from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new and bigger problem with the whole effort to find a verse source. Every source discussed so far deals with things that grow from the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even the best verse-based approach (the reading 'נטע רבעי') only covers things that are planted. Meat, eggs, and fish do not grow from planting, so no verse source reaches them. This problem breaks the entire derivation from verses.

keyTerms.meaning: Fourth-year planting (the reading that includes all planted fruit, not only vineyards)
That works well for... (but there is still a problem elsewhere)
Something that grows by being planted
From where does he learn it?

phrases.english: And according to the one who teaches 'fourth-year planting',
this works well for anything that is planted.
But things that are not planted,
such as meat, eggs, and fish,
from where does he learn it?

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not only against the vineyard reading. It hits even the wider נטע רבעי reading, because that reading still only covers planted things.
steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּתָנֵי נֶטַע רְבָעִי הָא תִּינַח כֹּל דְּבַר נְטִיעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After fixing the 'before eating' gap, the גמרא points out that the verse sources cannot cover foods that are not planted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The whole attempt to base the ברכה on verses (נטע רבעי / שבעת המינין)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: All the verse sources deal with produce of the ground, so they cannot obligate a ברכה on meat, eggs, or fish.

steps.title: The blessing is based on reason: no enjoyment without a blessing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops all the verse sources and concludes that the ברכה is a סברא: a person may not enjoy this world without a ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is a logical reason: a person is forbidden to enjoy this world without a ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up looking for a verse and gives the final answer. The duty to make a ברכה comes from plain logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא shows that the earlier attempts are put aside. The new basis is a סברא: the world belongs to ה׳, so taking pleasure from it without permission (a ברכה) is wrong. This reason covers every food, including meat, eggs, and fish.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical reason (not from a verse)
That he should benefit or enjoy

steps.whatToRemember: The basic duty to make ברכות on food is based on סברא: it is forbidden to enjoy this world without a ברכה.
steps.whyThisMatters: Because the source is logic, the rule covers every kind of pleasure from food, not only produce of the ground.

phrases.english: Rather, it is a logical reason:
a person is forbidden to benefit
from this world without a blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves step 33 (and leaves step 30's problem behind) by dropping the verse sources altogether.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברכה over food is a duty based on סברא, so it applies to all foods.

steps.title: A ברייתא: enjoying without a blessing is מעילה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא states the same rule and adds that whoever enjoys this world without a ברכה has committed מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A person is forbidden to enjoy this world without a ברכה. And anyone who enjoys this world without a ברכה has committed מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same rule as the סברא. It also adds how serious the sin is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא matches the סברא word for word, which supports it. It also compares the sin to מעילה, misusing something that belongs to the holy property. The world is ה׳'s, and the ברכה is what makes it permitted to us.

keyTerms.meaning: He committed מעילה, misuse of holy property

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A person is forbidden to benefit
from this world without a blessing.
And anyone who benefits from this world
without a blessing has committed misuse of the holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן אָסוּר לוֹ לָאָדָם שֶׁיֵּהָנֶה מִן הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה בְּלֹא בְּרָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the סברא of step 34 with a ברייתא and adds the idea of מעילה.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that one may not enjoy this world without a ברכה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא (תנו רבנן) with the identical wording, adding that it is מעילה

steps.title: What is his fix? Go to a חכם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: what is the remedy for someone who did this? The answer given is that he should go to a חכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is his remedy? He should go to a חכם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how a person who enjoyed without a ברכה can fix it, and answers that he should go to a חכם. This sets up the next question, which challenges this answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer gives a 'remedy' but does not say what the חכם will do. That gap is what the גמרא attacks in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: He should go to a sage

phrases.english: What is his remedy?
He should go to a sage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the ברייתא by asking about a remedy for the sin of מעילה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How a person can fix the wrong of enjoying without a ברכה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He should go to a חכם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The remedy for one who enjoyed without a ברכה is to go to a חכם.

steps.title: How can a חכם help after the sin is done?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is puzzled: what can the חכם do for him? He has already done the forbidden act.
steps.simpleTranslation: He should go to a חכם?! What will the חכם do for him? He has already done the forbidden thing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the remedy given in step 36. Going to a חכם afterward cannot undo the sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some prohibitions can be undone by a חכם, like releasing a vow. Eating without a ברכה is already finished, and nothing a חכם says can change that. So the 'remedy' seems to make no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: What will he do for him?

phrases.english: He should go to a sage?!
What will he do for him?
He has already done the prohibition!

steps.triggerLanguage: יֵלֵךְ אֵצֶל חָכָם מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the remedy given in step 36.
steps.kashyaTarget: The remedy 'יֵלֵךְ אֵצֶל חָכָם' given in step 36
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A completed sin cannot be undone, so going to a חכם afterward accomplishes nothing.

steps.title: רבא: go to a חכם beforehand and learn the blessings
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the ברייתא means to go to a חכם from the start and learn ברכות, so that one never comes to מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: He should go to a חכם at the start, and the חכם will teach him ברכות, so that he will not come to מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rereads the remedy from step 36. The 'remedy' is prevention, not repair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The remedy is not about fixing a past sin. It is advice to learn ברכות ahead of time from a חכם. Knowing the right ברכות protects a person from ever committing מעילה.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'remedy' of going to a חכם is prevention: learn ברכות in advance so you never enjoy this world without a ברכה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read רבא as saying the חכם can erase a sin already done. רבא's point is the opposite: the help comes before the eating.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
He should go to a sage from the start
and he will teach him blessings
so that he will not come to misuse of the holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא יֵלֵךְ אֵצֶל חָכָם מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 37 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the ברייתא's wording (prevention instead of repair)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Go to a חכם' means going after the sin to fix it, which makes no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means going to a חכם beforehand to learn ברכות, so as to avoid מעילה.

steps.title: שמואל: Enjoying Without a Blessing Is Like Using Holy Property
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: whoever enjoys this world without a ברכה is as if he enjoyed קדשי שמים, because the פסוק says 'The earth and all it contains belong to ה׳.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: Anyone who enjoys this world without a ברכה, it is as if he enjoyed things set aside as holy to Heaven. As the פסוק says: 'The earth and all it contains belong to ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement from שמואל that matches the ברייתא's idea of מעילה. Using the world without a ברכה is like using holy property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said that enjoying without a ברכה is מעילה. שמואל explains why: since everything belongs to ה׳, the whole world counts as His holy property. A ברכה is how a person gets permission to use it.

keyTerms.meaning: One who enjoys or gets benefit
Things set aside as holy to Heaven (הקדש)
As it is said (introduces a פסוק)

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the reason behind the ברייתא's harsh word מעילה. Benefiting from the world without a ברכה is treated like misusing הקדש.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Anyone who enjoys benefit from this world
without a blessing
it is as if he benefited from things consecrated to Heaven,
as it is said: 'The earth and all it contains belong to the Lord.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an אמורא's statement that fits with and explains the ברייתא's claim that enjoying without a ברכה is מעילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Enjoying this world without a ברכה is like benefiting from קדשי שמים, because the whole earth belongs to ה׳.

steps.title: Two Verses Contradict: Does the Earth Belong to God or to People?
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי points out a contradiction: one פסוק says the earth belongs to ה׳, and another says ה׳ gave the earth to people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי pointed out a contradiction. It is written: 'The earth and all it contains belong to ה׳.' And it is also written: 'The heavens are the heavens of ה׳, but the earth He gave to people.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי לוי sets two פסוקים side by side that seem to clash. This prepares the way for his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק, the same one שמואל used, says the earth is ה׳'s. The second פסוק says ה׳ handed the earth over to humans. Both cannot be simply true at the same time, so an explanation is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: He 'threw' two sources against each other, meaning he pointed out a contradiction

steps.confusionAlert: רבי לוי is not attacking שמואל. He raises the contradiction between the פסוקים only so he can solve it, and his solution teaches the same lesson about ברכות.

phrases.english: Rabbi Levi raised a contradiction:
It is written: 'The earth and all it contains belong to the Lord,'
and it is written: 'The heavens are the heavens of the Lord,
but the earth He gave to mankind'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the פסוק שמואל just quoted and sets it against another פסוק that seems to say the opposite.
steps.kashyaTarget: The פסוק 'לה׳ הארץ ומלואה' compared with 'והארץ נתן לבני אדם'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One פסוק says the earth is ה׳'s, and the other says it was given to people. These two claims seem to contradict each other.

steps.title: Resolution Begins: One Verse Describes Before the Blessing
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי answers that there is no contradiction: the פסוק saying the earth is ה׳'s describes the time before a ברכה is said.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here, in the פסוק 'The earth belongs to ה׳,' it is talking about before a ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי לוי starts to solve the contradiction by assigning each פסוק to a different time. Only the first half of his answer appears here, and the second half comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before a person makes a ברכה, the food still belongs to ה׳, so eating it is like using הקדש. This sets up the other half of the answer: after the ברכה, the earth is 'given to people.'

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no real contradiction
Here, meaning in this case or this פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: The answer is not finished yet. The matching half, 'here, after the ברכה,' is on the next amud.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, it refers to before a blessing,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers רבי לוי's contradiction by splitting the two פסוקים into different situations.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (כאן... כאן): each פסוק applies at a different stage, before or after the ברכה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two פסוקים seem to give opposite answers about who owns the earth.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לה׳ הארץ' describes the world before a ברכה, when everything still belongs to ה׳. The other half, about after the ברכה, continues on the next amud.
